reasoning: A hybrid strategy is chosen to balance deep cross-instance pattern recognition with rigorous feature attribution from established XAI tools. Autonomous analysis helps identify shared features across instances, while XAI tools quantify the model's dependence on each feature, revealing spurious correlations. This combination ensures both semantic insight and statistical robustness in identifying spurious predictors.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 42046) and list their values.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features with corresponding values across all three instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any of the shared features (e.g., education-num=9, marital-status=Married-civ-spouse) are semantically meaningful or likely to correlate with income class, or if they appear in large numbers of misclassified cases with no genuine relation.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A reasoned assessment on the semantic relevance of shared features to the correct class (income)

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides globally interpretable feature importance across all instances, helping detect features with high attribution even if semantically irrelevant. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local insight into prediction decisions, validating whether the model relies on spurious features. Sensitivity analysis confirms whether removing a feature causes significant prediction shifts, indicating its spurious influence. Together, these tools detect and validate shared spurious features that are both common and highly attributed.
